about: THE ONE PLACE THE THREE IMPLEMENTATIONS OF FieldSpec.text_format ARE COMPARED.
The server ENFORCES a declared format (app/services/stage_schema.py, _FORMATS, inside
coerce_value's scalar-text arm). Both clients render a PREVIEW of the same rule so the
ordinary mistake never costs a round trip on one bar of signal. A preview that disagrees with
the enforcement is a milder version of the defect this feature exists to end, so the three are
pinned against these rows rather than against a comment asking each side to stay in step.
WHY A CHECKED-IN TABLE AND NOT A PARITY COMMENT. Email is the control experiment. Its rule was
stated in three places -- a private regex in ArtisanForm.tsx, the same regex again as that
input's pattern attribute, and an arm of the Kotlin port of coerce_value -- with prose asking
them to agree. They did not: the web accepted an address with no @, Android refused it, the
server checked nothing, and nobody noticed. The only mechanism in this repository that
demonstrably holds three languages together is a checked-in fixture plus a test on each side
that reads it: that is structurally what
test_the_bundled_android_asset_matches_the_registry_it_was_dumped_from does for the schema, and
it is the only reason that asset cannot silently drift.
HOW TO READ A ROW. `value` is what a client posts or a designer types, AFTER clean_text and a
strip (coerce_value does both before any format runs). `error` is the exact sentence the format
answers, or null when the value is accepted. THE SENTENCES ARE PART OF THE CONTRACT: 'the same
checks, in the same order, with the same sentences' is written in three files in this
repository, and it is a UX promise -- a researcher who corrects a number on the handset must
read the same instruction on the laptop.
WHAT THESE ROWS DELIBERATELY DO NOT COVER:
* MASKING. participant.aadhaarNumber also declares store_masked, so an accepted full number
is STORED as 'XXXX XXXX <last four>'. That is a separate step, after this one, and it is
pinned by test_a_full_aadhaar_typed_into_the_carried_box_is_stored_as_the_mask.
* LENGTH. Bounds are FieldSpec.max_length, published to both clients as maxLength, and they
are checked BEFORE the format so an over-long answer keeps its own refusal rather than
being quietly shortened into a plausible mask.
* BLANK. Every *_error function in this repository answers null for a blank value; whether an
empty box is allowed is `required`'s question and validate_entry's.
* PEHCHAN. TextFormat.PEHCHAN exists and is enforceable, but NO FIELD DECLARES IT, on
purpose: participant.artisanCardNo carries a mask from hydration and pehchan_error ACCEPTS
a mask (fourteen alphanumerics, inside 4-32, no checksum to fail), so declaring it there
would be a no-op that looks like protection. See _pehchan_format_error.

`server_only` IS NOW EMPTY, AND THE KEY IS KEPT RATHER THAN DELETED. It held exactly one row -- PHONE_IN 'not a number' -- under the claim that no client control could produce it. That claim was true of the control and false of the column the control is filled from, so the row has moved into `vectors` and both clients now answer it. The key stays because the DISTINCTION is still real and the next row of that kind should go in it rather than being forced into `vectors`: a value no client can produce AND no client can be handed. The bar is higher than it looks, and the one row that was there did not clear it -- hydration hands a client whatever the record column holds.

WHERE THIS FILE LIVES, AND WHY IT IS NOT UNDER ANY ONE SIDE. At the repository root, so that no side owns it. A fixture inside a client's test resources reads as that client's fixture, and a fixture inside backend/tests reads as the server's -- and the whole claim being made here is that one rule has one answer.

divergences_to_reconcile: THREE DIVERGENCES HAVE BEEN RECORDED HERE AND ALL THREE ARE CLOSED. Kept rather than deleted:
each names a trap that will be walked into again, and the rows that pin them are in the table
above ('768 029', the PEHCHAN pair, '---' in three formats, and the four PHONE_IN rows).
1. PINCODE -- FIXED IN THE RULE, AND THEN FIXED AGAIN IN THE CONTROL THAT DRAWS IT.
The server checks the NORMALISED value: address.normalize_pincode strips separators, so
'768 029' is accepted and stored as typed. That is deliberate and is written at
participant.pincode -- values in exactly that shape are already in the column, typed by
somebody reading a card aloud. Both previews called pincodeValidationError on the RAW value,
which is right where that function lives (the record page's box strips non-digits as you
type, so a space cannot get into it) and wrong for a stage box, which shows whatever the
record held. Both now strip separators first --
stageFieldFormats.pincodeOrSpacedValidationError and DwTextFormats.pincodeError.
AND THAT WAS NOT THE WHOLE OF IT, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH READING. This entry used to end
'neither calls the record page's validator directly any more', and that was measured on the
dispatch table alone. StageAddressField -- the control the PIN code box actually mounts --
went on calling pincodeValidationError(own) on the raw stored value, and formatShownByControl
returns true for that role, so FieldInput's correct notice was SUPPRESSED in favour of the
wrong one. A hydrated '768 029' therefore drew a red line the server, the handset and
fieldFormatError all disagreed with, with aria-invalid absent and the collapsed-disclosure
count at zero. A rule with one implementation can still have two callers: whenever
formatShownByControl answers true, the control it names has to be checked, not just the
dispatch entry.
2. PEHCHAN -- FIXED IN THE CLIENTS, and it was harmless. The server measures the normalised value
(uppercased, non-alphanumerics removed), so pehchan_error's alnum arm can never fire there;
both clients measured the raw trimmed value and could return that first sentence. Both now
normalise first, which makes that arm unreachable on all three sides EXCEPT for a value that
normalises to nothing ('---'), where all three fall back to the raw string -- see 3.
All three ACCEPT 'XXXX XXXX 3456', which is precisely why no field declares this format and
why a mask-aware predicate is the prerequisite for attaching it to participant.artisanCardNo.
3. SEPARATORS ONLY -- FIXED IN THE CLIENTS, and it was a silent revert on three formats at once.
Every one of the server's three normalising entries (_aadhaar_format_error,
_pincode_format_error, _pehchan_format_error) has the same shape: normalise, and if that
leaves nothing, measure the RAW string. Both clients had ported the second half of each and
not the first, so a box holding '---' was accepted here and refused there -- no message, Save,
per-field refusal, save_stage restoring from previous, value back on the next GET with nothing
said. THE DIRECTION IS THE WHOLE POINT and this was the wrong one: a preview may be LOOSER
than the enforcement (one round trip lost, nothing wrong stored) and may never be TIGHTER (an
answer the server would take, refused on a stage nobody can get past) -- but 'looser' costs a
round trip only when the designer can see why, and a preview that stays silent about a value
the server will refuse is what makes a revert look like lost work.
ONE RESIDUAL, NAMED SO IT IS NOT MISTAKEN FOR AGREEMENT: pehchan_error on the server tests
str.isalnum(), which is true of Devanagari and every other script, while both clients test ASCII.
A value of nothing but non-ASCII letters therefore gets 'letters and digits only' on the clients
and the length sentence on the server. There is no row for it because NO FIELD DECLARES PEHCHAN;
the day participant.artisanCardNo does, that is the line to fix first and a row here is how to
prove it.

vectors.note: NO FORMAT DECLARED: the arm enforces nothing. This is the state of all but a handful of the registry's 570 fields and it must stay cheap and silent.

vectors.error: Aadhaar number must be 12 digits — remove any letters or symbols.
vectors.note: SEPARATORS ONLY, WHICH IS TYPEABLE: this is a plain text box, so a designer can leave three dashes in it. The dispatch entry the server actually enforces is _aadhaar_format_error, whose FIRST line is 'if normalize_aadhaar(text) is None: return aadhaar_error(text)' -- measured on the RAW string. Both clients had ported only its second half (aadhaar_or_mask_error), which opens with 'normalises to nothing -> no error', so both ACCEPTED this while the server refused it: no message on the box, Save pressed, the field refused, save_stage restoring it from previous, and the value back as it was on the next GET with nothing said. A silent revert, inside the feature written to end silent reverts.

THE LEGACY ARM, AND IT IS LOAD-BEARING. Artisan.phone has never had a server-side rule, so the table holds bare numbers written before the dial-code picker existed and hydration has been copying them into participant.phone ever since. Refusing this would put a permanent red error on every legacy roster row, over a value the designer cannot correct.

vectors.error: Enter a 10-digit number for +91.
vectors.note: TEN DIGITS, AND REFUSED ANYWAY. phone_digits strips everything that is not an ASCII digit before the count, so the 4-14 window bounds the DIGITS and says nothing about the string: this was accepted, stored and printed. max_length does not close it either (it is sixteen characters against a bound of twenty), so all three sides now also check the SHAPE -- an optional dial code, digits, and separators, nothing else. It cannot refuse anything either picker composes, because both write '+CC digits' and nothing else.

vectors.error: Enter a 10-digit number for +91.
vectors.note: MOVED HERE OUT OF server_only ON 2026-08-24, AND THE NOTE IT CARRIED THERE WAS WRONG IN AN INSTRUCTIVE WAY. It said 'no client can reach it', because both clients opened their phone rule with 'no digits -> no error' and a phone box only accepts digits. True of the CONTROL, false of the DATA: nothing has ever validated Artisan.phone, hydrate_entries copies it into participant.phone, and coerce_value re-coerces every field on every save. So a stored value like this refused on EVERY save while both previews called it clean, and PhoneField drew an EMPTY BOX for it (it renders only the digits it could parse) with FieldInput's notice suppressed because formatShownByControl says the control speaks for PHONE. Nothing on the page, and a silent revert on the next GET. Both clients now refuse a non-blank value with no digits, and PhoneField prints the stored string it cannot show.
